title: BlackBerry AtHoc Alerts Now Reach WhatsApp and Microsoft Teams
summary: BlackBerry AtHoc delivers alerts on WhatsApp and Microsoft Teams, reaching people in the apps they use.
body_markdown:
During a critical event, composing the message is rarely the hard part. Landing it is. A text from an unfamiliar short code often causes recipients to hesitate while they determine whether it is legitimate. An email sits behind dozens of others. A phone call reaches one person at a time. Meanwhile, many people are moving between two apps all day: a personal messaging app and a collaboration app.


BlackBerry® AtHoc® now delivers alerts to both. Operators can send alerts to WhatsApp and Microsoft Teams, along with SMS, email, voice, desktop pop-up, and mobile app push notifications.


## **Coverage, Not Capacity, Is the Limiting Factor**


Most organizations that run a critical event management platform already have channels that scale. What they lack is confidence that each person received each message on a channel they read and recognize. In practice, the gaps cluster around the same groups: distributed and multinational staff, where delivery rules and per-message costs vary by country; contractors and partners outside the corporate identity system; desk-based program staff whose attention lives in a collaboration app rather than an inbox; and anyone trained by years of spam to ignore unknown senders.


Adding channels helps only if the record stays consolidated. A channel that creates a second console to watch, or an incident that lives in a chat thread nobody reports on, makes the operator’s job harder during the worst hour of the year. That constraint shaped both integrations.


## **WhatsApp: A Channel People Already Use from a Sender They Can Verify**


For a large share of the world’s workforce, WhatsApp is the default space for messages that matter. BlackBerry AtHoc alerts arrive from a verified business profile, so recipients can see who is contacting them before deciding how to act. That removes the hesitation caused by an unrecognized number, saving valuable time during an evacuation or site closure.


Operators can include the alert title and body, response options recipients tap to report status, a location, and supported attachments such as a site protocol or an evacuation map. Locations and attachments arrive as their own WhatsApp messages alongside the alert.


Recipients opt in rather than being automatically enrolled. A user adds a WhatsApp number to their profile in AtHoc Self Service and acknowledges an information-sharing consent disclaimer. Only then can an alert reach them there. Consent is captured during onboarding, which matters for organizations that need to show how a personal channel came into scope.


Delivery is visible afterward. WhatsApp reports sent, accepted, delivered, and read states, where available, into BlackBerry AtHoc reporting and CSV exports. Operators can distinguish a message that left the platform from one that a person opened. That distinction is what tells a duty officer who still needs a phone call.


## **Microsoft Teams: Alerts Inside the App Already Open on the Desktop**


Three things make a Microsoft Teams alert land. First, it arrives in software that has been open since log-on. Second, it arrives through an app the organization’s administrators approved, installed, and pinned inside the organization’s Microsoft 365 tenant, so it reads as workplace communication rather than an unknown contact. Third, it behaves the same way on Teams desktop and Teams mobile, so staff at a workstation and staff moving through a facility receive the same alert and answer it the same way.


Operators choose whether to send the title alone or the title and body. Response options appear as choices the recipient can tap without leaving Teams, and those responses report back into the AtHoc alert record next to every other channel. When the scenario calls for it, an alert can carry location details, a link to authoritative guidance, or a conference bridge number.


For operators who work in Teams as much as their staff do, the AtHoc publisher app for Teams already supports publishing from inside a Teams chat using quick-publish templates. Target a single team and recipients also get a link to join the collaboration space where the response is being coordinated. The alert reaches people where they already work, while follow-on coordination happens in the same place.


## **What Does Not Change**


Both channels are personal devices on the user record, the same as a mobile number or email address. The operator publishing an alert uses the same templates, attribute and geospatial targeting, review and publish steps, alert history, and reports. There is no separate console for either channel and no version of an event that exists only in a chat window. Reach expands without changing governance.


## **Additive by Design**


These are additional lanes, not replacements. Channels fail for unrelated reasons, which is why running several together is worth the configuration effort. Cellular networks can congest during a site emergency. A collaboration platform depends on corporate identity and network paths, so if that platform is the incident, that lane is down. A personal messaging app depends on data connectivity. Used together, no single failure takes the notification with it. SMS, email, voice, and mobile app push stay exactly where they were.


It is worth being precise about what these channels are for. They carry notifications, instructions, and structured responses. Sensitive operational discussion belongs in a channel built for it. That is where BlackBerry® SecuSUITE® sits in the portfolio: certified voice and messaging for conversations that should never touch the consumer app ecosystem. The BlackBerry AtHoc platform’s job on WhatsApp and Teams is reach and accountability.


## **Where to Start**


-


Map populations to channels instead of enabling everything for everyone. Contractors, international staff, and desk-based teams have different reachable channels.


-


Turn on response options. A delivered alert with no response leaves the loop open, and the loop is the reason the platform exists.


-


V


alidate with a small group first, on both desktop and mobile, and confirm responses appear in reporting the way your duty officers expect.


-


Keep at least two channels live for any population you have to account for.


-


Write for the format. Titles and bodies are shorter on messaging channels than in email, so the instruction goes first and the context second.


## **Reach People Where They Are**


Critical event management is judged by whether the right people acted, not by how many messages were sent. Adding WhatsApp and Microsoft Teams puts alerts in front of populations that other channels may reach unevenly and keeps every response in the record operators already use.
